rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SPORTS SYSTEM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Establishing The National Academy Of Sports System
rows.abstract:
Aims to develop the athletic skills and talents of students and prepare them for a long-term career in sports.

Mandates the NAS System to offer a full scholarship on secondary education to natural-born Filipino citizens with considerable potential in sports. For the purposes of this Act, foundlings who are born in the Philippines and those who acquired Filipino citizenship by virtue of Sec. 4 of RA 9225, otherwise known as the “Citizenship Retention and Re-acquisition Act of 2003,” shall be considered natural-born Filipino citizens.

Provides for the construction and site of NAS at the New Clark City Sports Complex, Capas, Tarlac; creates a Board of Trustees which shall be headed by the DepEd Secretary; provides the powers and functions of the Board; exempts importation of sportswear, equipment, books, supplies, instruments, materials and goods, including donations to the NAS System from custom duty in accordance with the provisions of RA 10862.
rows.status: Republic Act RA11470 enacted on 2020-06-09

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE NUCLEAR REGULATORY FRAMEWORK, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE, THE PHILIPPINE NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Aims to provide cheaper electricity for Filipinos by utilizing cheap and reliable energy sources through establishing a regulatory body which shall also focused on the use and application of nuclear energy with a vast coverage that will touch on issues regarding public health and safety, and protection of the environment.

Seeks to create said autonomous regulatory body which shall exercise authority over all aspects of safety, security and safeguards involving nuclear and other radioactive materials, facilities and radiation generating equipment.

Proposes provisions which include but is not limited to the control of peaceful uses and application of nuclear energy in order to strengthen science and technology and boost industrial growth, harmonization of Philippines' nuclear regulatory structure with other countries and ensure consistency with the nation's obligations under relevant international instruments and modernize the nuclear civil liability and compensation regime in line with internationally-accepted standards.
rows.status: Substituted by HB10178

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE EXPORTATION OF BLACK SAND AND ITS DERIVATIVES IN ITS RAW FORM TO OTHER COUNTRIES
rows.abstract:
Intends to address potential revenue losses from black sand mining caused by unscrupulous companies who take advantage of the laxity by which permits are issued, which prompted the Mining Industry Coordination Council (MICC) had issued Resolution No. 4 or the \"Adoption of Immediate Measures to Address Black Sand Mining Operations in the Country.\"

Proposes to prohibit the exportation of black sand in its raw form and to require all black sand mining companies to institute, build, or lease advanced processing plants for magnetite within the province where they are conducting actual mining operation.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ELECTION OF SECTORAL REPRESENTATIVES TO THE LEGISLATIVE BODIES OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS
rows.abstract:
Proposes to resolve the unrealized provisions of the Party-List System Law and the Local Government Code which provides for sectoral representatives in local legislative bodies to consider the important role of the marginalized sectors in nation-building by ensuring their participation in crafting policies that involve the general and collective interest of the Filipinos.

Intends to bring into fruition the Constitution's vision of balanced, democratic and well represented 
local legislative bodies where sectoral representatives of workers or peasants, women, urban poor, 
indigenous people, persons with disabilities, and all other organizations which shall be identified in 
the future can now participate in the local elections.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE FILIPINO YOUTH INVOLVEMENT IN AGRICULTURE AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP
rows.abstract:
\"Young Agripreneurs Act of 2020\"
Aims to address the state of unemployment, underemployment and the condition of rural youths who are forced to work in urban communities.

Intends to create a  \"Youth Agricultural Hubs\" in provinces and highly urbanized cities which shall: 
be the center for trainings, assistance, and opportunities; monitor and evaluate programs, projects, 
and activities; and facilitate partnerships among stakeholders, in the promotion of youth involvement 
in agriculture.

Proposes the conduct of series of \"Youth Agripreneurship Trade Fairs\" showcasing the youth's agricultural products; and appropriates three percent (3%) of Internal Revenue Allotment of the LGU concerned for youth's hubs.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A COMPREHENSIVE POLICY ENABLING YOUTH PARTICIPATION IN ADOLESCENT PREGNANCY PREVENTION

"The Local Council Adolescent Act of 2020"
Aims to address the alarming increase of teenage pregnancy incidence among Filipino women which has brought serious consequences for teenagers involved and has affected every aspect of their lives, both their physical and mental well-being, during and after the baby is born.

Defines "Adolescent Pregnancy" as an individual belonging to the age group of 10-19 who is child-bearing; Seeks to create a comprehensive policy enabling youth participation in adolescent pregnancy prevention.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A MEDICAL SCHOLARSHIP AND RETURN SERVICE PROGRAM FOR DESERVING STUDENTS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to narrow down the doctor to population ratio, specifically in geographically isolated and
disadvantaged communities.

Intends to provide access to medical education of students aspiring to become doctors especially 
those who are financially disadvantaged; and to instill in them the importance of medical service 
to the country, especially in the underserved areas.

Mandates LGU's to provide necessary support to the integration program of physicians who will be
assigned to the LGU.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN THE ROLE OF PRIVATE BASIC EDUCATION IN THE PHILIPPINES BY CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE PARTNERSHIP IN PRIVATE EDUCATION BOARD, AND THE PARTNERSHIP FUND FOR PRIVATE EDUCATION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Proposes to create the Partnership in Private Education Board, attached to DepEd whose principal functions among others are to: develop, lead, and coordinate the government's efforts to strengthen the role of private educational institutions, and to expand such role in partnership with the relevant agencies of the national government; coordinate information activities designed to mobilize public support through volunteerism, special projects, demonstration pilots, ad public-private partnerships; and ensure that their activities, efforts and performance meet high standards of excellence and accountability.

Intends also to create the \"Partnership Fund for Private Education (PFPE), to be appropriated annually under the GAA for the purpose of financing assistance and partnership programs with private basic education institutions.

rows.abstract:
Seeks to clarify the definition of public services and public utilities; and institute an appropriate mechanism for fixing the rates, tolls, and the like based on a reasonable rate of return.
Intends to establish a process for vetting investments, and to provide safeguards should any investor pose a potential threat to national security involving critical infrastructure; and to empower the President to suspend or prohibit such transactions involving electricity transmission and distribution, water pipeline distribution, sewerage pipeline system, and telecommunications that threaten to impair the national security of the country.

rows.author: G050
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 183 AND 184 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract:
States that in the case of “False testimony in other cases and perjury in solemn affirmation”, the penalty of PRISION MAYOR IN ITS MINIMUM PERIOD TO PRISION MAYOR IN ITS MEDIUM PERIOD shall be imposed upon any person, who knowingly makes untruthful statements and shall testify under oath, or make an affidavit, upon any material matter before a competent person authorized to administer an oath in cases in which the law so requires.

Penalizes any person who shall incriminate or impute, through false testimony or untruthful statements under oath or through an affidavit, any person in the commission of a crime.

Provides further that if the offender is a public officer or employee, the penalty shall be imposed in its maximum period; shall suffer a fine not to exceed one million pesos; and perpetual absolute disqualification from holding any appointive or elective position.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2020-03-02

rows.author: I070
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 22, AN ACT PENALIZING THE MAKING OR DRAWING AND ISSUANCE OF A CHECK WITHOUT SUFFICIENT FUNDS OR CREDIT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to amend the \"Anti-Bouncing Check Law\" by increasing the prescribed jail term for the offenders who issue unfunded checks OR HAS CLOSED AN ACCOUNT, to an imprisonment of not less than thirty days but not more than SIX (6) years or by a fine of not less than but not more than double the amount of the check, or both such fine and imprisonment at the discretion of the court.

Proposes that if the reason for the dishonor of the check is the closure of the account, all the subsequent checks issued shall be deemed dishonored without the need of presentment; States that the penalty shall not be applicable for closure of accounts which are done in good faith or when the parties agreed in writing to revise the terms of payment.

Aims that the amended law will have more deterrent effect in issuing unfunded checks, and thereby significantly reduce the number of B.P.No.22 cases file in courts and to strengthen public confidence in checks as a negotiable instrument.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2020-03-02

rows.author: I051
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING ECOTAX ON BATTERIES
rows.abstract:
Aims to create economic incentives arising from environmental-friendly endeavors, usually levied on activities or products known to be harmful to the ecology; Intends to address the demand for more technical, advanced, and expensive public mechanisms for the collection and processing of electronic wastes; Seeks to reduce pollution and encourage the use of alternatives.

Proposes to impose an Ecotax (ecological tax) on Rechargeable Batteries equal to one percent (1%) and Disposable Batteries and other products with similar contents equal to three percent (3%) of the actual sale price; such Ecotax shall cover battery manufacturers, producers, and importers.
